the RRAT J1819–1458 is an X-ray pulsar with a 5.5-s period, and that it has a radio counterpart with a period of 3.1 s and a dispersion of 100 pc cm−3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no evidence that the RRAT J1819-14 is emitting in the optical.
we have shown that the optical emission is at most a few percent of the X-ray emission, but that the X-ray and radio emissions could have different spectral indices.
the optical emission of J1819- 1458 is at least 3 magnitudes fainter than the radio emission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radio bursts of RRATs are not associated with optical bursts.
optical observations of J1819- 1458 are not likely to reveal any optical counterparts to the radio bursts.
we have demonstrated the power of the simultaneous radio/optical approach to searching for optical bursts from RRATs, and we encourage other researchers to adopt a similar strategy.
